svg.aria-label: How to write 语: 9 strokes · 8 pen lifts · 9 movements
svg.title: Writing 语
svg.desc: 9 frames; frame N shows movements 1 to N of 语 (chinese), the movement being added drawn in ink over the finished letter, whose outline is read from _fonts/NotoSansSC-Subset.ttf. Stroke order after Hanzi Writer Data 语.json, ordered stroke paths and medians 1–9 (Hanzi Writer Data snapshot 68d10a4, updated from Make Me a Hanzi, 22 June 2019) <https://raw.githubusercontent.com/chanind/hanzi-writer-data/68d10a4b21150cae5e1ebbd223eed289cf32d90c/data/%E8%AF%AD.json>. Source note on variation: The cited PRC-order dataset supplies nine ordered strokes for 语. Medians 1–2 complete 讠 first, medians 3–6 complete 五, and medians 7–9 complete 口 with the bottom-closing stroke last. Make Me a Hanzi documents that its stroke paths are ordered in proper stroke order, its medians share the coordinate system used for stroke-order animation, and the project follows People's Republic of China stroke order. The ductus uses those ordered source medians directly; the vendored Noto Sans SC outline can differ in width and proportion from the Arphic-derived source graphics.
